title: Reducing capture work moved synchronization costs and did not establish a speedup
summary: Opportunity-only sampled scoring modestly improved the early semantic configuration, but ARC remained faster. Replacing query-index construction with slices moved much of its host wait to score readback rather than removing the cost.
scope: Dense Qwen3-4B BF16 eager simulated-agent experiments. The scoring-efficiency study covered nine lifecycles/405 exact requests; the separate slice/concatenate test covered four lifecycles/180 exact requests.
limitations: Single-run product comparisons and different closed-loop histories. Indexed search used its tiny-bank fallback in serving; forced replay had routing/build costs and only 88.02% mean top-8 recall. Inclusive host timers overlap and cannot be added as GPU compute savings.
decision: Retain the synchronization lesson. The slice/concatenate candidate was restored after no measured product gain; indexing and lower capture cadence were not qualified as general improvements.

chart.caption: Separate single-run studies and comparators; no pooled estimate or confidence interval.
